task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: I found your account. Let me verify a few more things on the line.

I've pulled up your account and checked the line — good news on the account side so far:

- **Customer:** John Smith (C1001), account status: **Active**
- **Affected line:** 555-123-2002 (L1002), status: **Active** — not suspended
- **Contract end date:** 2026-12-31 (still valid)
- **Bills:** No overdue bills (your latest bill is issued but not yet due/overdue)
- **Data usage:** 8.7 GB of 15 GB used this cycle — you're well under your limit
- **Roaming:** Already enabled on this line

So nothing on your account or line should be causing "No Service." That means we should look at the phone itself.

On your device, could you please check a couple of things for me?

1. **Look at the top of your screen (status bar).** Do you see an airplane ✈️ icon? If so, swipe down from the top to open Quick Settings and tap the airplane icon to turn Airplane Mode **off** — it turns off all wireless connections.
2. **How many signal bars do you see**, and does it show a network type (5G/4G/LTE)? Or does it say "No Signal"?
3. **Wi-Fi:** Are you connected to a home Wi-Fi network?

Let me know what you see and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my phone now.

turns.thought:
Yes, exactly — that's almost certainly the problem! The ✈️ icon means Airplane Mode is ON, which disconnects all wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so you'd get no signal at all. That matches your symptoms perfectly.

Here's how to turn it off:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** (once, and maybe a second time) to open the Quick Settings panel.
2. **Find the Airplane Mode tile** (it has the little airplane ✈️ icon). It's usually lit up/highlighted when it's on.
3. **Tap it once** so it turns gray/un-highlighted.

Once you do that, give it about 10–30 seconds and check the top of your screen again — you should see the signal bars come back, along with a network type like 5G or LTE.

Go ahead and try that, and let me know what you see afterward. If the bars come back, try making a quick call or opening a webpage to confirm it's working. If you still see "No Signal," we'll dig deeper together.

One quick note: your Wi-Fi is also off — once Airplane Mode is off, you can turn Wi-Fi back on the same way (tap the Wi-Fi tile in Quick Settings) so you can connect to your home network again. But let's tackle the cellular signal first.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn Airplane Mode off.

turns.thought:
Totally understandable — I know that's disappointing after trying the fix. But this is actually useful information: it tells us the issue is something other than Airplane Mode, so let's narrow it down.

Two things to try next, in order:

**Step 1 — Turn Mobile Data back on**
Airplane Mode sometimes leaves mobile data switched off even after it's disabled.
- Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings.
- Look for the **Mobile Data** tile (it often looks like two arrows pointing up/down, or is labeled "Mobile Data"). Tap it so it's **on/enabled**.
- Wait about 30 seconds and check whether the network type (5G/LTE) appears next to the bars.

**Step 2 — Restart your phone**
If there are still no bars after that, please do a full restart — this refreshes the phone's connection to the cell towers and fixes a lot of temporary glitches:
- Press and **hold the power button** (about 3 seconds).
- Tap **Restart / Reboot**.
- Wait for it to fully boot back up, then check the status bar again.

By the way, I re-checked things on my end while you did that: your line 555-123-2002 is **Active**, your contract runs through 2026-12-31, there are **no overdue bills**, and you've used only 8.7 GB of your 15 GB data allowance. So there's nothing on your account or line that should be blocking your service — it's something on the phone itself, which is very fixable.

Try those two steps and tell me exactly what the status bar shows afterward — particularly whether you see any bars or a network type like 5G/LTE. If it still says "No Signal," we'll move on to checking your SIM card and APN settings.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me start with turning mobile data back on.

turns.thought:
Yes, please go ahead and restart your phone now — that's the right next step.

Here's how:

1. **Press and hold the power button** (about 3 seconds) until the power menu appears on screen.
2. Tap **Restart** (or "Reboot"). If you only see "Power Off," tap that instead, wait about 30 seconds for it to fully shut down, then press and hold the power button again to turn it back on.
3. **Wait for the phone to fully boot up** — this usually takes a minute or so. Don't worry if it seems slow the first time.
4. Once it's back on and you've unlocked it, **look at the status bar at the top** and tell me exactly what you see:
   - Any signal bars? (none / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4)
   - Any network type like 5G, LTE, or 4G?
   - Does it still say "Data Disabled"?
   - Is the ✈️ airplane icon still gone?

A restart forces the phone to re-register with the cell towers from scratch, which resolves a lot of "No Signal" cases that toggling settings doesn't fix. It's our best shot before we start looking at the SIM card and APN settings.

Go ahead and take your time — I'll be here when you're back. Let me know what the status bar shows after the restart.

I hear you, and I'm sorry this has taken several tries. You've done everything right so far — and actually each thing we've ruled out is genuinely useful. Let's move on to the SIM card, which is the next most likely culprit.

**Step 1 — Reseat the SIM card**

A SIM that has come slightly loose in its tray is a very common cause of "No Signal," and re-seating it often fixes it instantly.

1. **Power the phone off completely** (hold the power button → Power Off). Always do this before touching the SIM.
2. **Find the SIM tray** — usually on the side of the phone. It has a tiny pinhole next to it.
3. **Insert the SIM eject tool** (the small metal pin that came in your phone box — a straightened paperclip works in a pinch) into the pinhole and **push gently but firmly** until the tray pops out slightly.
4. **Pull the tray out fully** and lift the SIM card out.
5. Take a quick look: is it seated flat in the tray? Any visible dirt or damage? If it looks dusty, **gently wipe the gold contacts with a clean, dry, soft cloth**.
6. **Place the SIM back in the tray**, making sure it's lying flat and aligned with the outline/notch.
7. **Push the tray back in** until it clicks flush with the phone body.
8. **Power the phone back on** and give it a minute, then check the status bar.

⚠️ **One important note about your device:** our records show your phone (Smartphone Pro Max) is **eSIM-capable**. If your phone uses an **eSIM** (a digital SIM — no physical card), then there's no tray to open, and this step won't apply. If you can't find a SIM tray or ejector hole anywhere on the phone, stop there and just tell me — we'll handle it differently.

**While I have you here** — one more thing worth ruling out on the account side, so you have the full picture: your line 555-123-2002 is confirmed **Active**, your contract runs through **2026-12-31**, and there's nothing blocking your service on our end. So this really is a device-level issue, and those are very fixable.

After you've done the SIM reseat, tell me what the status bar shows. If it's still "No Signal," our next step is checking your **APN settings** (the settings your phone uses to connect to our data network) — an incorrect APN is another very common cause, and resetting it to default often resolves it.

Take your time — no rush.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try reseating the SIM card.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry it hasn't clicked yet — I know four attempts with no change is genuinely wearing. But yes, APN is a good next step, and you've been doing great following along. Let me explain what it is first.

**What APN is:** APN stands for **Access Point Name**. Think of it as the "address" your phone uses to reach our mobile network for data and picture messaging. Normally you never think about it, but if it gets changed or corrupted, the phone can struggle to connect properly. Resetting it to the default is safe — it won't erase your photos, contacts, or apps.

**How to reset it** (these are the standard Android steps — your menus may be worded slightly differently):

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (on some phones this is **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **Mobile networks**).
4. Tap **Access Point Names** (sometimes just **APN**, and sometimes it's tucked under an **Advanced** section).
5. In the **top-right corner, tap the three dots ⋮** (or "More").
6. Tap **Reset to default**.
7. Confirm if it asks.
8. **Restart your phone** — this part is required, the new settings won't fully apply without it.

After it boots back up, check the status bar again and tell me what you see: any bars? A network type like 5G or LTE? Still "Data Disabled"?

**One more thing to look at while you're in Settings** — this one can matter a lot:

Your phone has a **network mode preference**, which tells it what kind of network to connect to. If it's set to an older mode like 2G or 3G, you can get weak or no data. While you're in **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network**, look for **Preferred network mode** (or "Network mode"). If it's set to anything other than 4G/5G, change it to **5G/4G preferred** or **5G/LTE auto**.

Try the APN reset plus the restart first, and make a note of what the network mode is currently set to. Let me know how it goes — and if we're still seeing "No Signal" after this, I'll get you connected with our technical support team directly rather than putting you through more steps here. You've been patient, and I don't want to keep guessing on your end.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check what my APN settings currently are first.

turns.thought:
Good question — and no, **don't reset it**. Here's why:

Your APN already shows a name ("internet") **and** an MMSC URL is present. Per our troubleshooting guidance, a reset is only recommended when the APN name shows as "Incorrect" or the MMSC URL is missing — and yours has neither problem. Resetting something that's already correct wouldn't help, and there's no reason to change it. Your network mode being set to "4G/5G preferred" is also exactly right.

So here's where we stand. We've now ruled out the standard causes:

Everything on your account and line is healthy, and we've worked through every device-side fix I'm able to walk you through. Since you're still getting "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," this needs deeper technical support — things like checking the SIM's provisioning status directly and possibly issuing a new SIM, which is beyond what I can do here.

I'm going to transfer you to our technical support team now so they can take it from here. I'll pass along everything we've tried so you won't have to repeat it all.
